content.intended_use: Establish the constant one-query necessity independently of positive-budget chain lower bounds.

proofs.full_local_argument: Fix arbitrary p>=2 integer and Lp,D,epsilon>0, M>epsilon. Set a=-D/2<b=D/2, X=[a,b] and x0=0. X is nonempty compact convex with diameter D and contains x0. Each F_s(x)=s M is globally C-infinity. For all x,y, (F_s(x)-F_s(y))(x-y)=0, establishing monotonicity. Every derivative of order j>=1 vanishes; since p-1>=1, |D^(p-1)F_s(x)-D^(p-1)F_s(y)|_op=0<=Lp|x-y|. Thus both are admissible for the supplied positive upper bound Lp. Because a!=b, positive strong monotonicity with parameter mu would require 0>=mu|a-b|^2, impossible for mu>0. There is no bound on operator values in this class that excludes M. Their full jets are exactly (s M,0,...,0). Now derive the cones. At a, z-a>=0 for every z in X, so every n<=0 satisfies n(z-a)<=0. Conversely, taking z=b forces n<=0. Hence N_X(a)=(-infinity,0]. At b, z-b<=0 for every z, so every n>=0 satisfies the inequality, and taking z=a forces n>=0; thus N_X(b)=[0,infinity). For a<x<b, taking z=a forces n>=0 while taking z=b forces n<=0, hence N_X(x)={0}. For F_+=M, at a choose n=-M<=0 to get residual zero. At an interior point only n=0 is allowed, giving residual M. At b all n>=0 give |M+n|>=M, with equality at n=0. Thus r_+(a)=0 and r_+(x)=M for x!=a. For F_-=-M, at b choose n=M>=0 to get zero. Interior points give residual M; at a, n<=0 gives |-M+n|>=M, with equality at n=0. Hence r_-(b)=0 and r_-(x)=M for x!=b. Since M>epsilon, the respective success sets are exactly {a} and {b}. Let A be any measurable zero-query feasible output rule with seed independent of the unknown operator. On the common public input its history is empty for either sign, so its output Y=psi(xi,empty) has one common probability law mu on X; coupling the same xi even gives equal outputs pointwise. Therefore q_+=mu({a}) and q_-=mu({b}). These measurable singleton events are disjoint because D>0, so q_++q_-=mu({a,b})<=1. Consequently at least one of the two fixed signs has success probability <=1/2. Selecting a sign with smaller probability depends only on A's law, not on a realized seed, and therefore produces a fixed hard instance. Both probabilities cannot be >=2/3. Since this construction works for every permitted positive parameter choice, any algorithm family successful on every admissible instance with probability >=2/3 must have worst-case budget at least one. Finally, querying at x0=0 once returns s M; M>0 makes its sign unambiguous. Output a for the positive value and b for the negative value. In either case n=-F_s lies in the computed endpoint cone and cancels F_s exactly. This proves the one-query escape for the pair and shows why the argument asserts no positive-budget hardness. If M<=epsilon, all the computed residuals are <=epsilon; this explains the strict M>epsilon condition.

assumptions: Fix integer p>=2 and positive Lp,D,epsilon; choose any M>epsilon.
The public input is (1,X,0,p,Lp,D,epsilon), identical for the two signs. A common M and family promise may also be given without weakening the conclusion.

The randomized algorithm makes zero calls to the unknown operator; its arbitrary measurable feasible output is psi(xi,empty history) in X, and xi is independent of the unknown sign. Unlimited measurable internal computation using public information is allowed.
The admissible model requires C^(p-1) regularity on an open neighborhood, monotonicity on X, and Lip(D^(p-1)F)<=Lp; it imposes no separate bound on |F| or positive strong-monotonicity parameter.
statement.conclusion: Both F_s belong to the admissible class, with derivative Lipschitz constant zero and no positive strong monotonicity. Their epsilon-solution sets are {a} for s=+1 and {b} for s=-1. Every common zero-query output law has success probabilities q_+ and q_- satisfying q_++q_-<=1, so min(q_+,q_-)<=1/2<2/3. Therefore any uniform successful worst-case oracle budget is at least one. For this pair only, a single value query reveals s and permits an exact endpoint solution; no N>=1 or epsilon-power hardness follows.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Work in R with norm |.| and usual inner product. Let a=-D/2, b=D/2, X=[a,b], x0=0 and F_s(x)=s M on R for s in {+1,-1}. Define N_X(x)={n:n(z-x)<=0 for all z in X} and r_s(x)=dist(0,F_s(x)+N_X(x)). A feasible exact order-p call returns (F_s(x),DF_s(x),...,D^(p-1)F_s(x))=(s M,0,...,0). For general multilinear derivatives the norm is sup_{|u_i|<=1}|T[u_1,...,u_j]|.
statement.parameter_domains: d=1; p integer >=2; Lp,D,epsilon strictly positive; finite M>epsilon. No restriction on Lp D^p/epsilon and no high-dimensional regime is required.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer p>=2, every Lp,D,epsilon>0, every M>epsilon, and every such randomized zero-query rule A on the common public input, there exists a fixed s in {+1,-1}, chosen independently of the realized seed, for which P_xi[r_s(A(xi))<=epsilon]<=1/2. Equivalently, no zero-query algorithm family achieves per-instance success >=2/3 over all admissible instances. The sign need not be sampled in execution; only the algorithm seed supplies the probability in the conclusion.

summary: For every fixed p>=2 and positive Lp,D,epsilon, arbitrary randomized zero-query feasible output cannot succeed with probability >=2/3 on every admissible monotone VI. A two-instance argument gives a fixed member with success <=1/2.
title: Lemma 11.5: at least one query is necessary
